caveats: Sample: 1,000 consecutive orthodontic patients before treatment from Ricketts' private practice (p. 333): Class I 399, Class II div. 1 367, Class II div. 2 217, Class III 17; 546 female, 454 male; ages 3 to 44, mean 8.9 years, 901 of them aged 3–14 (61 + 497 + 343, Chart 1). Not a normal or ideal sample.

Lower lip, whole sample (not entered; ruling P36a, its age rows are entered instead): 0.3 mm ahead of the E plane, SD 3.0 mm, 1,000 cases (p. 343). It is the only E-line value in this paper with an SD; the age rows (Chart 2) have none.
Upper lip: −0.7 mm in the first 800 cases, no SD, no age breakdown (p. 343); entered as one row covering ages 3–44.

Chart 2 (p. 339) gives age-group means with no SD; the n on those rows is each age group's count in Chart 1 (p. 333). Chart 2's 'Adult' row is Chart 1's 19–44 group. There is no row between 18 and 19 (bands are in completed years, so 18.9 is in 15–18).

Not entered, ruling P10 (Ricketts' own analysis uses ricketts1981; these are pre-treatment sample values): facial angle 85.4° SD 3.7° (p. 335); mandibular plane 25.7° SD 5.9°, range −11° to +46° (p. 337); convexity A to N–Pog 4.1 mm SD 2.8 mm (p. 338), by age 5.5, 4.4, 3.7, 2.5, 1.7 mm (Chart 2); lower incisor tip to A–Pog 0.5 mm SD 2.7 mm, range +10 to −10 mm (p. 341; Fig. 11 prints 0.4 ± 2.7), by age −0.9, +0.4, +0.7, 0.0, 0.0 mm (Chart 2); lower incisor to A–Pog 20.5° SD 6.4° (p. 341, Fig. 12); upper incisor to A–Pog 5.7 mm SD 3 mm (Fig. 13).

Not in the catalogue: XY axis (Ba–N to S–Gn), mean +3.0 from 90°, SD 3° (p. 336); N–S–Ba 129.6°, range 114–144°, n 200 (p. 346); S–Gn–N 35°, range 25–42°, n 200 (p. 346); condyle axis to Ba–N −5.7° from 90°, range −19 to +20°, n 200 (p. 349).
Means and SDs are reported 'in round figures' where practical (p. 333). Film scale and head position are not stated; ethnicity is not stated (Pacific Palisades, California, private practice).
